words.headline: Radiators Ghosted Us: No-Heat Calls Nearly Double on a 46° Morning
words.blurb: No-heat complaints hit 1,568, almost twice the usual 827, as the low dipped to 46 degrees. Whole-building outages led the chill with 809 reports, more than double a typical Tuesday.

boroughs.Bronx: Home repairs led with 759 calls, and 488 more were asking where the heat went.
boroughs.Brooklyn: Parking wars ruled the borough with 1,297 calls about curbs, hydrants and driveways.
boroughs.Manhattan: Home repairs topped the list at 580, with no heat and noise tied at 400 each.
boroughs.Queens: Parking wars led by a mile: 910 reports from the land of the blocked driveway.
boroughs.Staten Island: Parking wars came first with 93 calls, and street fixes followed with 55.

rare_finds.name: News gathering: flying too low
rare_finds.quip: There's an official form for a news helicopter being too low. Somewhere a clerk holds a ruler up to the sky, deciding what counts as too low.

rare_finds.name: Driver complaint - passenger: cell phone use
rare_finds.quip: What's the deal with this one? The city has a box to check for a phone in the back seat. Bureaucracy has officially entered the group chat.

rare_finds.name: Sidewalk zone blocked: siamese water connection
rare_finds.quip: New Yorkers will step over anything, except apparently a fire department pipe fitting. That one finally got paperwork.
